title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. C is a k-linear category of '½-simplicial bimodules', meaning semi-simplicial objects with a bimodule structure. C_0 is the additive full subcategory of the ∂-perfect ones. The previous page computed Homs between exterior powers Λ^iΨ_α and Λ^iΦ_α, and between the twisted objects Φ_α(i,n). Here those computations are abstracted into a 'résumé' with axioms.

The axioms concern a cochain complex Φ^0 → Φ^1 → … → Φ^i --∂_i--> Φ^{i+1} → … in C_0:
(a) The complex is acyclic in C.
(b) Hom(Φ^i,Φ^j) is:
- k·id if j=i;
- k·∂_i if j=i+1;
- 0 otherwise.
So the Φ^i form a directed linear chain whose only non-trivial maps are scalars and the differential. This is the same Hom pattern as the Koszul pieces Λ^iΦ.
(c) Put Ψ^i = Z^i = Ker ∂_i, which equals Coker ∂_{i-1}, with Ψ^0 = Φ^0. This gives canonical short exact sequences (*) 0 → Ψ^{i-1} --p_i--> Φ^i --u_i--> Ψ^i → 0, with ∂_i = p_{i+1} ∘ u_i.

Derived Homs. Composing with the epimorphisms u and the monomorphisms p embeds each Hom into a Hom between Φ's. Reading off (b):
- Hom(Ψ^i,Ψ^j) = k·id if j=i, and 0 otherwise.
- Hom(Φ^i,Ψ^j) = k·u_i if j=i, and 0 otherwise.
- Hom(Ψ^i,Φ^j) = k·∂_i if j=i+1, plus k·id when i=j=0, and 0 otherwise.

(d) For u ∈ k−0 and i ≥ 1, let L(i,u) be the pushout of (*) along u·id on Ψ^{i-1}. Its class is u·e_i, where e_i is the class of Φ^i in Ext^1(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}). Note L(i,1) = Φ^i.

Homs between the L's.
- Any map L(i,·) → L(j,·) respects the two-step filtrations. This uses Hom(Ψ^{i-1},Ψ^j) = 0 for j ≠ i−1, in particular for j = i.
- If j ≠ i, the induced maps on the graded pieces vanish. So Hom(L(i,u),L(j,·)) ≅ Hom(Ψ^i,Ψ^{j-1}), which is k if j = i+1 and 0 otherwise.
- If j = i, a map induces p·id on the sub and q·id on the quotient. A filler α exists iff q^*(e_{i,v}) − p_*(e_{i,u}) = 0 in Ext^1(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}).

Next page. Under hypothesis (C), that e_i spans Ext^1_{C_0}(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}), the condition becomes the single linear equation qm = pn. α is unique because Hom(Ψ^i,Ψ^{i-1}) = 0. Hence Hom(L(i,n),L(i,m)) ≅ k.

Purpose. This is a dévissage: abstracting the Koszul/exterior-power building blocks of ∂-perfect objects into an axiomatic chain, presumably toward classifying objects of C_0 or their multiplicative structures by such pieces.
errors: For u ∈ k−0 the pushout along the automorphism u·id gives a middle object isomorphic to Φ^i itself; only the extension structure changes, not the object. So L(i,u) ≅ Φ^i, and Hom(L(i,n),L(i,m)) ≅ End(Φ^i) ≅ k follows immediately from (b). The filler/Ext computation and hypothesis (C) are unnecessary for this conclusion. They would matter only if n or m could vanish in k (e.g. char p, or a Z-linear setting), which is excluded here by u ∈ k−0.

On the next page the gcd normalisation m' = m/(m,n), n' = n/(m,n) is superfluous over a field. It suggests Grothendieck was thinking of n, m as integers, possibly with a Z-form or positive characteristic in mind. It also tacitly assumes p ≠ 0 when writing q/p.
The case-list for Hom(Ψ^i,Φ^j) needs the separate exception i=j=0 (because Ψ^0 = Φ^0). Grothendieck adds it, but the general formula '0 if j ≠ i+1' is literally false without it.
Minor: in (c) the kernel/cokernel Ψ^i is taken in C. It is not stated that Ψ^i lies in C_0, yet hypothesis (C) uses Ext^1_{C_0}.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of a chain of objects Φ^0→Φ^1→… with Hom(Φ^i,Φ^j) = k·id, k·∂ or 0 (a directed 'linear' category with relations ∂∂=0), modelled on the Koszul pieces Λ^iΦ
ideas.modern_name: Strong exceptional sequence / directed category of a linear A_n quiver with relations (Koszul-type); compare Beilinson's Λ^i-pieces

ideas.what: Splitting the acyclic complex into canonical short exact sequences 0→Z^{i-1}→Φ^i→Z^i→0 and computing Homs between cycles
ideas.modern_name: Standard dévissage of an acyclic complex into short exact sequences

ideas.what: Twisted extensions L(i,u) obtained by pushing out along u·id; a morphism with scalars (p,q) on the graded pieces exists iff q^*e − p_*e = 0
ideas.modern_name: Baer pushout / functoriality of Ext^1 for extension classes

missed.claim: The 'résumé' isolates exactly the Hom pattern of a strong exceptional / Koszul chain in an abstract k-linear category, in a context of ½-simplicial ∂-perfect objects, c. 1975-76. This is close in spirit to the later theory of exceptional collections and Koszul duality, but stays at the level of Hom-computations on this page.
missed.quote: Hom(Φ^{(i)},Φ^{(j)}) ≃ 0 si j≠i,i+1 ; ≃ k (engendré par id) si j=i ; ≃ k (engendré par ∂_i) si j=i+1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck using an exceptional-sequence-style axiomatics for dévissage. Mathematically it is routine and contains nothing beyond standard homological algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean axiomatic summary with routine Hom/Ext computations. Its main mathematical conclusion is trivially true, since L(i,u) ≅ Φ^i for invertible u. The only mildly interesting feature is the exceptional-chain style axiomatization in an unpublished 1975-76 context.
transcription_corrections: Left margin note reads roughly 'unicité de (b)' or 'unicité de Φ'; it is attached to item (c) and is uncertain.
'la structure d'catégorie est respectée' should read 'la structure d'extension est respectée par les hom L(i,–)→L(j,–)'.
'les flèches entre les cokernels' is more likely 'les flèches entre les extrémités' (the maps on Ψ^{i-1}→Ψ^{j-1} and Ψ^i→Ψ^j), which are zero for j≠i.
The last line should be q^*(e_{i,v}) − p_*(e_{i,u}), where e_{i,u} and e_{i,v} define the extensions L(i,u) and L(i,v). It is not 'e_{j,-}'.
In the case j=i the target in the image is L(i,v), not L(i,u) again; the Hom under study is Hom(L(i,u),L(i,v)).
The right-margin annotation near the top ('on a aussi …') sketches a diagram Ψ^{i-1}→Ψ^{j-1}, Ψ^i→Ψ^j, i.e. a morphism of extensions.
